reflection.text:
Acquiring the high dose first (1 uM w_df2909f8b4) was decisive: tub_glcm_contrast z=+108.2 with tub_std z=+32.4 and tub_mean z=+25.1 indicated bright, textured bundling rather than tubulin loss, and the mid dose (0.03 uM w_13ba1079c0) already showed the same pattern at z=+62.9. What was imperfect was class overlap in the k-neighbour comparison (6/10 stabilizers, 4/10 destabilizers) and the non-specific cues of lower density/cell number and decreased nuc_form_factor (z=-26.2 to -27.9), which are shared by other mitotic arrests and could have sustained Aurora or Eg5 alternatives if tubulin intensity had been weaker.

The review text calling this a clean win for "Microtubule destabilizers" was a mislabel contradicted by its own 4-well tally and by the unblinding to docetaxel with ChEMBL Tubulin stabiliser mechanism; trusting the per-well similarities and quantitative bundling features over that label was why the run stayed correct.
what_was_right: High-dose tubulin texture and intensity increases (tub_glcm_contrast +108.2 to +115.0, tub_std +32.4 to +38.8, tub_mean +25.1 to +29.7) correctly pointed to bundling/stabilization, not loss.

Microscopist report of lower density with tubulin bundles converged with quantitative features to correctly downweight Aurora kinase and Eg5 inhibitors.
what_was_wrong: k-neighbour split of 6/10 stabilizers vs 4/10 destabilizers showed residual stabilizer-destabilizer confusion, likely from shared mitotic nuclear shape change (nuc_form_factor -26 to -28).

Review critique misnamed the winner as "Microtubule destabilizers" despite unanimous stabilizer votes, which would have been misleading if taken literally.

# MuseCell dossier · specimen s_0ed866d71e

Run `run_b55b1185302a` · blinded · 2026-10-31 19:34 UTC · models: scientist muse-spark-1.3, microscopist muse-spark-1.3, reviewer muse-wonder-1.0, segmentation classical (scikit-image), provider meta, atlas ResNet50 (ImageNet) + TVN, agent v5

## Hypothesis history

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.95); key evidence e9, e5, e2, e7, e8.

Why: Unanimous 4/4 NSC stabilizer vote, high similarity, replicated bright bundling features and visual bundles.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Washout plus acetylated-tubulin immunofluorescence and live EB-comet assay to test for persistent bundled stable microtubules versus depolymerization, with phospho-H3 mitotic index.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

## Unblinding

Compound: **docetaxel** (PubChem CID [148124](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/148124))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Tubulin inhibitor; Tubulin stabiliser

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule stabilizers**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (4/4). The Scientist's own call was **Microtubule stabilizers** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

Acquiring the high dose first (1 uM w_df2909f8b4) was decisive: tub_glcm_contrast z=+108.2 with tub_std z=+32.4 and tub_mean z=+25.1 indicated bright, textured bundling rather than tubulin loss, and the mid dose (0.03 uM w_13ba1079c0) already showed the same pattern at z=+62.9. Replication at 0.1 and 0.3 uM with z=+115.0 and +104.0 plus unanimous NSC votes for Microtubule stabilizers (2/2 then 4/4, similarities 0.842-0.871) and visual bundles made the 0.95 conclusion well supported and consistent with taxane stabilization literature (PMID 36876916).

What was imperfect was class overlap in the k-neighbour comparison (6/10 stabilizers, 4/10 destabilizers) and the non-specific cues of lower density/cell number and decreased nuc_form_factor (z=-26.2 to -27.9), which are shared by other mitotic arrests and could have sustained Aurora or Eg5 alternatives if tubulin intensity had been weaker.

The review text calling this a clean win for "Microtubule destabilizers" was a mislabel contradicted by its own 4-well tally and by the unblinding to docetaxel with ChEMBL Tubulin stabiliser mechanism; trusting the per-well similarities and quantitative bundling features over that label was why the run stayed correct.

What was right:
- High-dose tubulin texture and intensity increases (tub_glcm_contrast +108.2 to +115.0, tub_std +32.4 to +38.8, tub_mean +25.1 to +29.7) correctly pointed to bundling/stabilization, not loss.
- Dose continuity from 0.03 to 1 uM with NSC 4/4 votes for Microtubule stabilizers at 0.842-0.871 similarity correctly built confidence.
- Microscopist report of lower density with tubulin bundles converged with quantitative features to correctly downweight Aurora kinase and Eg5 inhibitors.

What was wrong or missed:
- k-neighbour split of 6/10 stabilizers vs 4/10 destabilizers showed residual stabilizer-destabilizer confusion, likely from shared mitotic nuclear shape change (nuc_form_factor -26 to -28).
- Cell-count/density drop alone was non-specific for antimitotics and did not discriminate stabilizers from destabilizers.
- Review critique misnamed the winner as "Microtubule destabilizers" despite unanimous stabilizer votes, which would have been misleading if taken literally.

Proposed next experiment: Washout test with acetylated-tubulin immunofluorescence and live EB1-comet imaging plus phospho-H3 mitotic index to prove persistent bundled stable microtubules versus depolymerization.
